hero.tagline: Where starlight whispers through the swirling firmament

today.heading: Even stones remember the silence before creation

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Chandra's ancient light upon the tide
moon.intro: Tulips close their petals at night under the Moon’s gaze, folding inward like a meditation. Yet at dawn they open again — a daily resurrection that mirrors the lunar cycle of death and rebirth.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: The ego: dust that thinks itself a mountain
philosophy.intro: A lily does not compete with the lily beside it. It simply blooms. Nature offers no hierarchy of flowers — each opens to the light in its own time, in its own way. The ego cannot comprehend this peace.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: The garment worn for a season, then cast off
gita.intro: The Gita teaches that the body is like a garment — worn for a season, then cast off. Tulips bloom for mere days, yet their brief radiance is no less real than the oak’s centuries. Duration does not determine significance.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: Between two eternities of stillness, the dance
shiva.intro: Before Shiva dances, there is silence. After Shiva dances, there is silence. The dance itself is the universe — a brief, brilliant interval between two eternities of stillness. The lily floats on still water, between two eternities of flow.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: The alchemy of perception: making the invisible seen
art.intro: Lilies transform still water into a mirror of sky. The artist does the same — taking the mundane and, through the alchemy of perception, revealing the extraordinary that was always there.
